items.q: What does it cost to paint a house in Redmond?

a.text: Redmond exteriors typically run $4,500 to $10,000 and interiors $3,200 to $25,000. Redmond splits cleanly into two very different pricing pictures. Education Hill, Grass Lawn, and the older neighborhoods near downtown have mature homes with wood siding and real prep requirements. Redmond Ridge and the newer developments east of town are largely fiber cement and engineered siding on builder-grade original coatings.
a.html: Redmond exteriors typically run $4,500 to $10,000 and interiors $3,200 to $25,000. Redmond splits cleanly into two very different pricing pictures. Education Hill, Grass Lawn, and the older neighborhoods near downtown have mature homes with wood siding and real prep requirements. Redmond Ridge and the newer developments east of town are largely fiber cement and engineered siding on builder-grade original coatings.

a.text: Newer does not automatically mean cheaper. Builder-grade paint on a fifteen-year-old home is often at the end of its service life all at once, across every elevation, which makes for a larger job than a well-maintained older home needing one exposed side addressed.
a.html: Newer does not automatically mean cheaper. Builder-grade paint on a fifteen-year-old home is often at the end of its service life all at once, across every elevation, which makes for a larger job than a well-maintained older home needing one exposed side addressed.

a.text: Yes — all Redmond neighborhoods, plus Union Hill, Overlake, and Sammamish Valley.

a.text: Redmond Ridge and several newer Redmond communities have architectural review requirements and approved color palettes. We work within them regularly and can prepare the color documentation your committee needs.

items.q: Our home is builder-grade construction from the 2000s. Is repainting different?

a.text: Somewhat, and it is worth knowing before you get bids. Production builders typically apply a single coat of contractor-grade paint over primer. It looks fine for a decade, then fails broadly rather than gradually — chalking and fading across whole elevations at once.
a.html: Somewhat, and it is worth knowing before you get bids. Production builders typically apply a single coat of contractor-grade paint over primer. It looks fine for a decade, then fails broadly rather than gradually — chalking and fading across whole elevations at once.

a.text: The good news is that the substrate underneath is usually sound. Fiber cement and engineered siding hold up well, so most of these projects are wash, prime bare areas, caulk, and apply two coats of quality coating. The result typically outlasts the original by a wide margin, because the original was never specified to last.

items.q: When should exterior painting happen in Redmond?

a.text: May through October, with June through August the most reliable stretch. Redmond runs slightly drier than Issaquah but the same constraints apply: surface temperature above roughly 38°F through cure, and no overnight dew on a fresh coat.

a.text: Interiors are year-round. Winter is a good time to do interior work — scheduling is open, and it keeps the summer calendar free for the exterior work that can only happen then.

nodes.text: More About Redmond
Redmond: Where Nature, Innovation, and Community Collide

In the heart of the Pacific Northwest, Redmond, Washington is a city alive with technological innovation, breathtaking natural beauty, and a strong sense of community. With a population of over 77,000 residents, Redmond is often referred to as the Bicycle Capital of the Northwest.
nodes.html: In the heart of the Pacific Northwest, Redmond, Washington is a city alive with technological innovation, breathtaking natural beauty, and a strong sense of community. With a population of over 77,000 residents, Redmond is often referred to as the Bicycle Capital of the Northwest.

nodes.text: Rooted in History, Geared Towards the Future

Redmond's history can be traced back to the late 1800s, when it was established as a small logging community. The city's name is derived from James W. Redmond, a prominent early settler and railroad developer. Today, Redmond is undeniably synonymous with technology, being the worldwide headquarters of Microsoft and the birthplace of numerous other tech giants.
